record.paper_title: On some open questions in bilinear quantum control
record.context_brief: Time-optimal transfer under an L1 control budget
record.original_question: Fix a bilinear quantum system dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ with first and second eigenstates φ_1 and φ_2 of the drift operator A. Suppose one imposes an a priori upper bound on the L^1 norm of the control u. Under that control-budget constraint, what is the smallest possible transfer time needed to steer the system from the first eigenstate φ_1 to the second eigenstate φ_2?

evidence.quote: For weakly-coupled systems, it can be easily proved (see [31]) that an a priori bound on the L1 norm of the control is not compatible with approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time.
Question 3: An upper bound on the L1 norm of the control being given, what is the smallest possible time needed to transfer a given system (A, B) from the first eigenstate of A to the second one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bilinear quantum control system on a complex Hilbert space H of the form

  i dψ/dt = (A + u(t) B) ψ,

where A is a self-adjoint operator (the drift Hamiltonian) with pure point spectrum, B is a self-adjoint operator (the control Hamiltonian), u: [0,T] → ℝ is a scalar, measurable control, and ψ(t) ∈ H satisfies ‖ψ(t)‖ = 1. Let φ_1 and φ_2 denote eigenvectors of A associated with its first and second eigenvalues, respectively, and assume the pair (A,B) is such that φ_1 can be steered (exactly or approximately, up to a global phase) to φ_2 by some admissible control.

Given a fixed constant K > 0, define the admissible class of controls

  𝒰_K = { u : [0,T] → ℝ measurable, T > 0, ∫_0^T |u(t)| dt ≤ K }.

Determine

  T*(K) := inf { T > 0 : ∃ u ∈ 𝒰_K with support in [0,T] such that the solution ψ of the system with ψ(0) = φ_1 satisfies ψ(T) = e^{iθ} φ_2 for some θ ∈ ℝ }

(equivalently, in the approximate-controllability setting, the infimum of T such that ψ(T) can be made arbitrarily close to the orbit of φ_2). Compute or characterize T*(K) as a function of K, and in particular for "weakly coupled" systems (where an a priori L^1 bound on u is known to be incompatible with controllability in arbitrarily small time).
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show ongoing work on L^p (especially L^1) costs for steering bilinear quantum systems between eigenstates of the drift, with explicit optimal L^1-costs computed only on examples and L^1 bounds derived for generic targets in weakly coupled systems. No source found that gives the minimal transfer time as a function of an a priori L^1 budget for general (A,B); the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Weakly Coupled Systems in Quantum Control
status_evidence.snippet: Weakly coupled systems ... L1-bounds of the controls for generic initial and target states are provided.
status_evidence.claim: L^1 control bounds are studied for weakly coupled bilinear quantum systems, but minimal time under such a budget is not characterized.

status_evidence.title: Which notion of energy for bilinear quantum systems?
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit optimal costs for the L1 norm are computed on examples.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal L^1 costs are computed only in examples, indicating no general formula for minimal-time transfer under an L^1 bound.
